description: Molybdenum is a chemical element with symbol Mo and atomic number 42. It is a silvery-grey metal that does not occur naturally as a free metal on Earth but is found only in oxidized states in minerals. The element was discovered in 1778 by Carl Wilhelm Scheele and first isolated as a metal in 1781 by Peter Jacob Hjelm.
uses: About 80% of world molybdenum production is used in steel alloys, including high-strength alloys and superalloys, because it readily forms hard, stable carbides. Approximately 14% of world production is used in molybdenum compounds serving as pigments and catalysts. Molybdenum is also essential for biological processes, particularly in nitrogen fixation enzymes in bacteria and cyanobacteria, and is essential for all higher eukaryotic organisms including humans.
characteristics: Molybdenum is a silvery-grey metal with a Mohs hardness of 5.5 and has the sixth-highest melting point of any element at 2,623 °C. It has one of the lowest coefficients of thermal expansion among commercially used metals and does not visibly react with oxygen or water at room temperature. Most molybdenum compounds have low solubility in water, and the element is a transition metal with an electronegativity of 2.16 on the Pauling scale.
